content.thinking:
I'm planning out the full character module in one pass, designing an Overwatch-style support cyborg medic around 1.8m tall with a skeleton covering hips, spine, chest, neck, head, jaw, arms, and legs, plus a healing staff held in the right hand that reaches down to touch the floor for stability.

I'm choosing a palette of white armor, dark graphite, mid gray, a teal-green healing accent, and warm skin tone for the face, then sketching the hips, spine, and neck chains with specific coordinate points and joint names to build out the rig manually.

Now I'm defining the head and jaw joints with explicit world coordinates instead of local axes to avoid confusion, setting the head center position and sizing it with a slightly elongated scale appropriate for hero proportions.

For the face, I'm designing a half-cyborg look: a white helmet dome covering the upper/back of the head, exposed skin on the lower face, and a glowing visor slit over one eye for readability instead of literal eye geometry. I'm also sketching helper functions for building boxes and panels, considering rounded geometry for a more polished mechanical look.

Planning the torso construction now using a swept path along spine coordinates, with a radius function to taper the shape from hips to shoulders.

For color, I'm leaning graphite undersuit tones with flat painted shading rather than cel-shading, since Overwatch's style favors clean, smooth gradients.

Writing shading helper function...

Now I'm planning arm placement and pose—a slight A-pose with the staff held in the right hand, and sketching out shoulder-to-elbow joint positions and lengths for the chain.

I'll settle on 4 points per arm chain (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand) using polyline segments for exact corners, parented to the spine joint, with tapering radii along the sweep.

For armor layering, I'm planning an asymmetric split: the left arm goes fully cybernetic with graphite/white panels and teal seams, while the right arm stays organic with a suit overlay, plus shoulder pads and forearm bracers as separate attached shapes. For hands I'll build a palm box with simple finger capsule chains and a rigid thumb, satisfying the "digits" rig requirement without needing ten fully independent chains.

Now I'm working out finger placement: each hand gets five two-joint finger chains positioned relative to the wrist using a direction vector and lateral offsets along the body's front-back axis, curling slightly forward to match the A-pose with palms facing inward toward the torso.

Actually, let me position the bent right arm holding a vertical staff: shoulder, elbow, and wrist coordinates leading the forearm forward then curving into a grip around the staff at roughly x=-0.42, z=0.34-0.36, with fingers wrapping around at a small radius.

Calculating finger positions wrapping around the staff...

Setting up the leg joint chains next: hip, knee, ankle, and toe for each leg with their coordinates, plus sweep radii tapering down toward the foot for a natural limb shape.

For the feet, I'm planning big white boots built from separate parts — an ankle box and a toe box joined together.

Still shaping foot geometry...

I'm placing the head center around y=1.74 with radius giving a top near 1.88, accepting some slack against the 1.85 target since exact measurement isn't feasible. Checking leg proportions with hips at 0.95, knee at 0.5, ankle at 0.1, giving a reasonable total leg length, then starting to work out the hip and torso sweep path and joint positions.

Still writing torso sweep...

Adjusting the plate centering so it protrudes just slightly past the torso surface, keeping corners sharp with no smoothing. For the chest emblem I'm thinking of a glowing teal cross with trim, avoiding anything resembling an actual game logo since a medical cross is generic enough.

Now I'm planning the back unit: a boxy medical pack with teal lights and antenna rods positioned behind the torso, plus pauldron spheres on the shoulders riding the arm bones, with a teal trim ring around each shoulder joint for detail.

For the collar I'm planning a lathed ring shape at the neck base, with a dark cyborg neck and white collar ring, using a lathe helper to generate the solid torus outline. Then I'm moving on to the head: a skin-colored sphere topped with a partial-sphere helmet shell.

For the visor I'm sweeping a curved tube shape across the eye area using catmull points, giving it a dark outer band and a thinner glowing teal strip layered just in front of it.

I'm refining the visor's bulge shape and considering a glowing strip across it, then weighing whether to give the character visible organic eyes (like Ana or Baptiste) instead of a fully opaque visor for better facial readability—leaning toward one eye organic and glowing on the other side for a cybernetic look.

Computing eye placements: right eye organic (white sclera, dark iris) and left eye cybernetic with a glowing teal ring, plus eyebrows and a cheek plate on the left side, skipping the full visor in favor of a brow guard. I'm calculating sphere positions and scaling for the eye geometry to sit correctly on the curved face surface.

Now I'm working out the nose wedge, mouth capsule, and chin/jaw placement relative to the skull sphere, adjusting positions and scales so each feature sits flush against the head's curved surface.

I'll nudge the mouth position against the jaw sphere's surface and settle on a warm brown skin tone for the paint. For hair, I'm planning a full helmet-style cap in white with a teal stripe, plus cyber headphone-like ear discs on both sides.

Working out the helmet geometry so it covers the back and sides without hiding the eyes, adjusting the sphere's angular range so it wraps correctly around the head...

Checking coverage: cap edge at y=1.80 sits just above the eyes and brow line, and the skull sphere radius there is smaller than the cap radius, so the cap fully conceals that region. I'm also adding a back piece covering the occipital area via the phi π..2π, theta 1.57..2.3 range.

A back plate risks exposing open edges or interior holes since material is likely single-sided, so I'll skip it and instead rely on the cap alone, extending its vertical angle to about 100° so it wraps further around the sides and back without leaving bald skin visible, checking how far the front edge dips as a result.

Testing this geometry: shifting the cap's center back slightly and expanding theta further makes the front edge recede into the skull surface at the brow but pop back out above the equator, so I'm checking whether the hairline sits correctly relative to the skull's curvature at different heights to avoid either clipping through the face or leaving a visible gap.

This naturally forms a hairline-like boundary where the cap emerges from the skull around the front, giving a visor-brim effect I'll accept. For safety I'll also add a thin brow band swept around the head at the forehead line using a loop path on the skull surface, giving a teal-white trim.

I'm adding a lifted headband loop on the skull surface, which may get partially hidden by the cap in back but will show at the front -- then simplifying rather than adding a torus rim. For ears, I'm placing small dark cylinder "cyber ear cup" shapes at the ear positions, rotated to align along the head's axis.

On the left side I'm adding a larger cup plus a teal ring torus facing outward, and an antenna rod with a tiny glow sphere tip curving from the cup up and back. For the staff held in the right hand, I'm planning a vertical shaft running from floor to about head height, with a caduceus-style design at the top.

Writing staff geometry...

Now I'm working out the precise joint coordinates for the right arm and staff placement—shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand positions—adjusting the staff's z-offset so it nestles correctly inside the palm sphere without poking through the surface.

I'm also sizing the palm as a small box and stacking four fingers along it with slight y-offsets, then figuring out where the thumb wraps around the opposite side of the hand.

Now I'm working out the wrap trajectory for the fingers—placing points along an arc on the inner side of the hand so they curl naturally around the staff at different angles.

For the thumb, I'm doing the opposite, computing points on the outer side so it opposes the fingers properly, then adding a base joint to connect it back to the palm.

Now I'm picking skin tones: dark graphite gloves for the right hand, white/graphite cyber plating with dark joints for the left. I'm also setting the staff radius and finger-wrap radius to keep things proportioned, then laying out the left arm's shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand positions with approximate hand dimensions.

Working out palm orientation by aiming the hand box along the wrist-to-fingertip vector, then placing finger base points spread laterally along that hand direction.

Naming each joint by finger, side, and segment index, then planning the arm radius profiles: a graphite cyber-plated left arm with exposed mechanical joints versus a dark suited right arm with teal piping, both built from tapered sweeps with armor segment splits.

Rather than guessing at the joint parameterization, I'll just use the path's closest-point lookup to find the elbow's t-value directly from the actual joint positions, which avoids ambiguity.

For the sweep I'll run the arm radius taper only up to the wrist, keeping the hand span as a thinner continuation, then set up matching leg sweeps that taper to the ankle. After that I'll handle chain parenting for the joints.

Still adding joints and checking spine path alignment...

Adding belt loops, pouches, buckle and pelvis plate, then setting up helper functions for armor boxes...

I need to be explicit about bone assignments so parts like the backpack correctly follow the chest joint rather than defaulting to the nearest one, and I should import the proper types like PartOptions and Joint while keeping unused imports out to avoid errors.

For textures, I'm planning an SVG-based emblem decal for the chest plate using a ring-and-plus design with a teal outline and alpha cutout, applied via a plane with glow so it reads in the part's own colors. I'm also considering a painted panel-line texture for the white armor plates to add surface detail.

Writing armor paint function...

Defining the color palette...

Writing armor paint helper with seams and grime...

I'm sketching keyframe curves for torso radii along the body path, mapping parameter t to rx/ry pairs for waist, chest, and hip widths, then setting up a pelvis box with its own dimensions.

For legs I'm defining joint chains—hip, knee, ankle, toe—with positions and tapering radii, chaining sweep segments between them so the shin smoothly blends at the ankle before ending in a rounded foot tip.

Now I'm working out boot attachments: the ankle joint anchors the cuff while the foot tip anchors the toe parts, and I'm building the cuff as a vertical sweep rod with tapering radius and white end caps.

Writing boot geometry...

Defining the band helper function...

Now I'm designing the limb details: cyber forearm with exposed pistons on the left arm versus a graphite sleeve with elbow pad on the right, differentiated pauldrons (tech vent vs medical cross), and a chest-mounted backpack box with teal side tanks.

Adding tank glow strips, antenna rods, and cable sweeps from pack to hips...

Then moving to a high collar ring and chest emblem with horizontal abdominal plate bands.

Still writing belt loop geometry and shoulder strap harness drape paths...

Actually, since the chest plate would conflict with straps, I'll skip the harness and just keep hip pouches and the belt. I'm also deciding to skip the back sling, then moving on to facial details like eyebrows, a cyber eye ring, and a small cheek-mounted cyber plate, working out its position relative to the skull's surface geometry.

I'm placing the cyber plate as a thin rotated box angled roughly 35 degrees to follow the face's curve, and I'm treating the skull itself as a smooth sphere shape with skin shading, deferring finer facial detail to separate parts. Now I'm working out the eye placements, with the organic eye on one side and the cyber eye on the other, centering their vertical position on the face.

I'm computing eyebrow positions as small boxes offset from center, solving for where they sit against the curved skull surface so they hug the forehead correctly, and I'm double-checking how the cap dome's rim aligns with the skull front so it tucks in rather than floating outside the head shape.

To hide that gap I need a rim band covering the edge, so I'm considering a flattened torus scaled into an ellipse shape, rotated to lie flat and sized to match the skull's curvature at that height.

Working out the scale and rotation order for the torus so the tube stays thin and the band hugs the rim correctly, then deciding to keep it a plain gunmetal color rather than teal to match the rest of the piece. Next I want to add a crest fin on top, extruded from a side-profile outline along the z-axis.

Now I'm positioning that fin at the dome's peak so it sinks slightly into the surface, then placing the ear cups symmetrically on either side with their radius and depth tuned to nest against the skull without clipping. I'm assigning bone attachments for the skull-related parts and deciding to skip extra hair tufts and visible teeth since the mouth is just a simple line.

For the staff, I'm building it as a rigid child attached to the right hand, laying out the shaft, a flat-capped foot touching the floor, leather grip bands wrapped around the hand position, and a few decorative bands along the shaft with a glowing teal ring near the top, now working out the lathe profile for the collar just below the staff's head.

Above the collar I'm sweeping four curved prongs outward in pairs along both the x and z axes to form a crescent-like holder, tipped with small glowing teal spheres, then placing a glowing teal orb with a brighter inner core at the center, and adding a tilted halo torus around it.

Writing gyro rings and wing geometry...

Checking edges for self-intersections...

Actually, I'll simplify to a safer three-feather polygon shape and apply it with minimal smoothing, thin thickness, positioned near the collar with a slight tilt.

Keeping the x and y axes non-orthogonal should be fine for the wing orientation. I still need to add the glove detail for the hand holding the staff, and I'll keep the wings plain white with just a touch of teal edging. Now I'm defining the staff joint attached to the right hand.

Adding more joint details...

For the chest, I'm placing a small emblem plane slightly offset from the chest plate surface so it doesn't clip, using a textured material that carries its own coloring, then adding a glow effect. For the hips, I'm adding leather pouch boxes on each side, and considering reusing a cross decal texture for a small decorative detail on them.

Now I'm designing two SVG icon textures: a teal plus-shaped cross for pouches, pauldrons, and boots, and a more detailed emblem combining a dark hexagon ring with a teal plus and small white circle inside for the chest badge. I'm positioning an emblem decal on the right pauldron, orienting it to match the dome surface's outward-facing normal direction near the shoulder.

Asserting non-null since the hit should land given the docs example. I should also add some chest plate surface details like small vent strips, and plan the left forearm's cyber details with exposed rods running along the armor gaps.

Now I'm defining a function to build a relaxed hand shape, computing palm and finger positions based on the wrist-to-hand-end direction vector, with specific joint coordinates for the left arm.

Still writing hand joint positions...

Now I'm setting up the glove colors — leather dark for the right hand, steel and graphite tones for the cyber left hand — before moving into the arm-building function and starting the overall build() export structure.

Skipping the unused rng import, I'm defining a small vector helper and laying out the skeleton joints, starting with the hips as root and a spine chain of points running upward.

Continuing the rig...

Now setting up the arm chains, defining shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand joints along a polyline path for the left arm, then starting the mirrored points for the right arm.

Defining arm armor sweeps...

Now I'm attaching shoulder joints to the pauldrons, then building out the torso with a swept curve for the suit body and a separately extruded chest plate shape positioned near the chest bone.

Working out the plate's depth position relative to the torso curve, placing it around z=.145-.18 with the emblem decal sitting at the front face around .183, then positioning the plate vertically to span y 1.135-1.415.

Now I'm adding small teal accent rods near the shoulder slopes of the plate, plus abdomen detailing using thin sweep loops at the belly for GUN-style lines, and sketching out pelvis geometry with hip guard boxes, a codpiece plate, and pouches before moving on to the neck collar band.

Now I'm placing a high neck collar ring in white, then building out leg armor: thigh plates as tapered sweeps overlapping the pelvis, a knee pad sphere scaled to sit at the joint, and shin greave sweeps tapering down from knee to ankle.

For the legs I'm figuring out the joint chain path for hip, knee, and ankle, placing boots using the ankle bone reference, then setting up helper functions and types for building the parts list with box and sweep geometry.

Setting up box helper...

Still defining helper types...

Writing the lighting helper function...

I'll skip seams for rounded parts and define distinct paint variants for armor, suit, gun, skin, boots, leather, and steel, each adding its own texture treatment. Now I'm moving on to building the emblem texture as an SVG shape.

Adding decal placement and body parts...

Still placing pouch decals and buckle geometry...

Now I'm adding the belt sweep with a leather loop and steel rivets spaced around it, then starting on a back pack box attached near the chest bone.

Below that I'm placing a gun-shaped lower box, teal gas tanks modeled as capsules with a pearl body and teal lathed band accents, a glowing teal indicator light bar, and antenna rods sticking up from the pack.

For hoses I'm sweeping a thin dark tube along a Catmull-Rom curve running from the pack down toward the hip, keeping it bone-attached to the chest for a static pose. Now I'm shifting focus to the staff, arms, jaw, and eyes, then assembling the full code while double-checking variable units stay consistent.

Writing finger wrap geometry...

Adding knuckle details, a back-of-hand armor plate, and wiring up the joint references for both hands, plus setting up a glowing palm emitter disc facing inward on the left hand.

Working out the mouth sweep path and cheek details, then designing the cyber left eye with a teal glow ring, dark lens sphere, and inner glow positioned against the skull's curvature.

Now I'm calculating the right eye geometry mirrored at x=-0.04: sclera, iris, pupil, and highlight sphere positions, nudging depths so each layer stays visibly in front of the last, plus setting up the eyelids.

Moving on to brows, nose, ears, and the cyborg jaw/cheek plate details, skipping facial hair for simplicity, then building the cap geometry as a partial sphere scaled to fit the head with armor coloring, plus a teal stripe arc sweeping across the top using a curve path.

Still computing dome surface points...

Those open straight edges at the sides would show as thin backface-culled walls, letting the viewer see into the skull's interior, so I'll avoid that by adding a nape hair patch instead — a small dark sphere positioned behind the skull, sized and offset so it tucks into the back without poking through the front or sides.

Good enough for hair, I decide, and settle on a dark brown hex for it. Now I'm moving on to writing the actual file, defining bone chains for decor like the head joint, and setting up default nearest-joint behavior since bones are supplied almost everywhere. I start building the leg structure for each side symmetrically, defining a polyline of hip/knee/ankle/foot points and chaining them into joints with named roles and contact points.

Writing leg sweep radii...

Adding leg armor pieces...

Adding boot details now, with cuff bands and toe caps, then double-checking joint parenting so the staff attaches after the arms, and verifying rod and glow helpers work correctly with bone-attached parts.
